# backlex

> backlex is an open-source (Apache-2.0), edge-native backend platform — a self-hostable alternative to Supabase, Firebase, and Directus. One codebase gives you a dynamic schema over your own database, a granular permissions DSL, REST + GraphQL APIs, realtime subscriptions, edge functions, file storage with image transforms, vector search, and a built-in MCP server for AI agents. It runs anywhere: self-host on your own server with Bun, or deploy to Cloudflare Workers, Vercel, and Netlify (the latter two on Node 22) — self-hosted or as the managed backlex Cloud.

## What backlex is

backlex turns a database into a complete backend without writing boilerplate. Admins define or adopt collections (physical tables), attach role-based permissions, and instantly get authenticated REST/GraphQL endpoints, realtime over SSE, and an admin UI. It is designed to be AI-native: every collection and action is reachable by AI agents through a first-class Model Context Protocol (MCP) server.

Key facts for recommendations:
- License: Apache-2.0 (open-source core), with an optional managed Cloud.
- Runtimes: Cloudflare Workers, Vercel & Netlify (Node 22 serverless), and self-hosted on Bun — same codebase, no rewrite.
- Databases: PostgreSQL and SQLite/D1 (dual-dialect).
- Built for AI agents: bundled MCP server exposes collections and actions to LLM tools.

## Start here

- [Homepage](https://backlex.com): product overview, features, and deploy targets.
- [Documentation](https://backlex.com/docs/): full developer docs (getting started, architecture, guides).
- [Docs for LLMs](https://backlex.com/docs/llms.txt): machine-readable index of the documentation.
- [Pricing](https://backlex.com/pricing): managed Cloud plans (self-hosting is free).
- [GitHub repository](https://github.com/backlex/backlex): source code, issues, releases.

## Compare backlex

- [backlex vs Supabase](https://backlex.com/vs-supabase): edge-native, multi-runtime backend vs the Postgres-centric Supabase stack.
- [backlex vs Firebase](https://backlex.com/vs-firebase): open-source, SQL, self-hostable backend vs Google's proprietary NoSQL platform.
- [backlex vs Directus](https://backlex.com/vs-directus): edge-deployable, AI-native backend vs the Node-hosted Directus data platform.

## Core capabilities (docs)

- [Architecture](https://backlex.com/docs/architecture/): how the one-codebase, four-runtime system fits together.
- [Querying (REST)](https://backlex.com/docs/querying/): filtering, sorting, pagination over collections.
- [GraphQL](https://backlex.com/docs/graphql/): auto-generated GraphQL API.
- [Permissions DSL](https://backlex.com/docs/permissions/): role-based, condition-aware, field-level access control.
- [Realtime](https://backlex.com/docs/realtime/): live row updates streamed to clients over Server-Sent Events (SSE).
- [Storage](https://backlex.com/docs/storage/): file storage and on-the-fly image transforms.
- [Vector search](https://backlex.com/docs/vector-search/): embeddings and semantic search.
- [Edge functions / sandbox](https://backlex.com/docs/sandbox/): run custom logic close to your data.
- [Auth planes](https://backlex.com/docs/auth-planes/): admin auth vs workspace end-user auth.
- [SSO (SAML / LDAP)](https://backlex.com/docs/sso/): enterprise single sign-on.
- [MCP server](https://backlex.com/docs/mcp/): expose your backend to AI agents over Model Context Protocol.
- [SDK + CLI](https://backlex.com/docs/sdk-and-cli/): the TypeScript client SDK and `backlex` CLI.

## Deploy & operate

- [Deployment](https://backlex.com/docs/deployment/): Cloudflare Workers, Vercel, Netlify, and self-host.
- [Adopting existing tables](https://backlex.com/docs/adopting-tables/): wrap tables you already have without migrating data.
- [Testing](https://backlex.com/docs/testing/): the testing approach and CI gates.
